topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D Geometry to 3D Space

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors and Planes
lecture_lines: Vectors have both magnitude and direction.
Planes are flat surfaces in space.
The Right-Hand Rule defines orthogonal direction.
animations: Draw two vectors in 3D, colored #FFFFFF and labeled 'v1', 'v2'.
Construct a plane passing through both vectors, colored #808080.
Use the Right-Hand Rule [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hand.svg] to show orthogonal direction, colored #FF00FF.

sections.title: The 2D Pseudo-Cross Product
lecture_lines: Calculate the signed area of parallelograms.
It indicates orientation, clockwise or counter-clockwise.
animations: Display two 2D vectors in a plane, labeled #FFFFFF.
Draw a parallelogram formed by vectors, labeled #FFA500.
Highlight the signed area with text 'Orientation', #00FFFF.

sections.title: The 3D Cross Product: Definition and Geometric Meaning
lecture_lines: Cross product produces a new vector.
Result is perpendicular to input vectors.
animations: Render two vectors in 3D, labeled #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gyroscope.svg]
Show perpendicular output vector, labeled #FF00FF.
Scale parallelogram area to output magnitude, #FFA500.
Show rotation path around the output vector, #00FF00.
Rotate the entire system for clarity, #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hinge.svg]

sections.title: Computational Method: The Determinant
animations: Display 3x3 matrix skeleton, labeled #FFFFFF.
Place unit vectors i, j, k in row 1, #FFFF00.
Show expansion steps for i, j, and k, #00FFFF.
Highlight final algebraic vector result, #FF0000.
Demonstrate with a simple example vector using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg], #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Torque
lecture_lines: Force applied to lever arm vectors.
animations: Display a rotating lever arm, labeled #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lever.svg]
Apply force vector at the end of lever, #FF0000.
Show resulting torque vector, labeled #00FF00.
Highlight relationship between force and torque, #FFA500.
Apply to a spinning mechanical gear, #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gear.svg]
